purpose: Separate evidence for pooled UBO update strategy from evidence for the proposed 16 MiB Unreal OpenGL pool capacity.

source.binary: libUnreal.so copied from the live TFT PBE process mapping

cvar_registration.name: OpenGL.UBOPoolSize
cvar_registration.help: Size of the UBO pool, 0 disables UBO Pool

uniform_buffer_allocation.observation: The stripped OpenGL code allocates a GL uniform buffer using a size held in its allocation object.
uniform_buffer_allocation.qualification: Static data flow did not prove that this particular allocation object's size is the OpenGL.UBOPoolSize value; do not use this xref as capacity validation.

official_api_cross_check.use: Comparative mechanism context only; current Epic API documentation is not proof of the exact stripped Riot implementation.

synthetic_scope.what_the_probe_establishes: On the attested ANGLE-to-Vulkan path, one map/fill plus per-draw range binding is consistently faster than one glBufferSubData update per draw for these exact working sets.
what_the_probe_does_not_establish: TFT frame rate or late-PvP frame tails
TFT's live uniform-buffer bytes per frame or in-flight pool pressure
that Unreal uses the probe's exact orphan/map policy
that 16 MiB is the smallest sufficient capacity

decision.why_no_smaller_profile_was_added: Without live pool-pressure or fallback evidence, a smaller pool is not known to be safer; it can trade memory for exhaustion, fallback, or reuse stalls.
required_sequence: Run at least two independent, profile-attested late-PvP Performance Max control sessions and two 16 MiB candidate sessions under stable host power and thermal brackets.
Require improved median and p95/p99 combat frame time with no rendering, crash, or memory regression before treating pool enablement as effective.
Only after an efficacy win, compare smaller 4/8 MiB capacities against 16 MiB to find the lowest non-regressing capacity.
